title: Self-serve evidence redaction pipeline for customer attestations
creator: Ethan Miller
description:
Goal: build a self-serve pipeline that allows enterprise customers to request CAIQ/SIG-style attestation exports with automatic sensitive-data redaction and an auditable minimal-evidence bundle. The feature should reduce manual effort for Sales/SEs while preventing leakage of internal secrets and minimizing legal review time.

Scope and deliverables:
- Customer UI flow in Console: request attestation -> choose scope (service, region, deployment type) -> choose disclosure level (Full / Minimized / Redacted) -> submit and receive downloadable bundle.
- Server-side pipeline: intake request, run structured mapping from CAIQ answers -> locate evidence artifacts (Confluence/Drive/PRs/logs) -> apply automated redaction heuristics + allow optional manual review by Redwood trust ops.
- Redaction artifacts: produce a ZIP with redacted PDF/MD, redaction metadata (line-level rationale), cryptographic hash of original and redacted artifacts, and an audit log entry. Support KMS-HSM signing for enterprise customers (opt-in).
- Pricing hook: flag heavy-attestation exports (batch > 10 docs or > 5MB evidence) to increment attestation credit consumption and emit billing event.
- Ops: dashboard for request latency, false-positive redaction rate, manual review queue size, and cost estimate per request.

Key acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow in Console that returns a redacted bundle within SLA: 95% under 24 hours with automated-only path, 95% under 72 hours if manual review required.
- Redaction precision: automated redaction false-positive rate < 5% on a curated test set and recall (sensitive items removed) > 98%.
- Audit trail: every export has immutable audit record, cryptographic hashes, and optional HSM signature for enterprise customers.
- Billing integration: requests correctly emit attestation_credit events in billing pipeline and reflect in customer invoices.

Trade-offs and technical notes:
- Heuristic redaction vs ML redaction: ML reduces manual review but increases ops complexity and model drift risk. Initial launch will use deterministic rules + regex + metadata matching; ML-based classification will be tracked as backlog (ENG-ML-1).
- Performance vs safety: aggressive redaction reduces disclosure risk but may over-redact useful evidence. Provide a customer-facing toggle (Minimized vs Full) and a clear changelog of what was removed.
- Legal sign-off: Legal prefers manual QA for redacted exports for top 10 enterprise customers; provide 'fast-path' for customers who sign a liability waiver.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal Redwood teams + 2 pilot customers (SE-managed). Validate redaction heuristics and audit trail. Timeline: 2 weeks.
- Beta: self-serve UI enabled for invited customers with attestation credits billing experiment. Timeline: 4 weeks.
- GA: open to all customers, with pricing documented and console UX stabilized. Timeline: 8-10 weeks.

Metrics to measure success:
- Reduction in manual SE/Legal time per attestation (target: -60% for pilot customers).
- Number of attestation credits consumed per month and average cost per export.
- Customer satisfaction (CSAT on attestation flow >= 4.2/5).

Notes on dataset and privacy:
- Pipeline must never include raw secret artifacts. Evidence connectors will mount scoped read-only views and enforce redact-first policy.
- Store redaction metadata for 90 days by default; configurable retention for enterprise customers.
